card.title: May the owl process your personal data?
card.body: So that the owl can also enter your name, tax ID, date of birth, address, bank details (IBAN), marital status, the details about your partner and children, and your religious affiliation, these details are sent to the language model that writes the answer. That can be a model by {{providers}}, depending on the setup, your model choice and outages; processing may take place in the USA. Your consent covers all of these providers. Religious affiliation is a special category of personal data (Art. 9 GDPR); by choosing “Allow” you also expressly consent to this. Without consent the owl masks these details and you enter them yourself in the forms. You can withdraw your consent at any time under Profile → Privacy.

deviceSessions.sessionData: Every sign-in stores that session’s IP address and device type (User-Agent). When you sign in from a new device via QR code, you see that data on the confirmation screen and in your device list in Profile, where you can sign each session out individually.
deviceSessions.geoIp: For QR-code sign-in we additionally resolve the requesting device's IP address to a country (e.g. "Germany"), never anything more precise — this helps you tell a stranger's request apart from your own. That resolution runs entirely on our own EU servers, against a self-hosted database we keep up to date; your IP address never leaves our infrastructure and is never sent to a third-party provider. If the database is out of date or an address can't be matched, we honestly show "Region unknown" rather than guess.

taggeld.frage: Where did the daily benefit in the gross wage (Ziffer 8) come from?
taggeld.hilfe: Only the daily benefit of an insurance is tax-free and deducted from the gross wage. A remark such as “KK-Taggeld Verrechnung” on the Lohnausweis points to the insurance. If a private insurance pays you directly, it is not in the Lohnausweis: then “no daily benefit”.

quelle.krankentaggeldversicherung: Daily sickness benefit insurance (offset with the wage)
quelle.lohnfortzahlung: Continued pay by the employer without an insurance
quelle.beides: Both (the insurance pays part, the employer tops up)

betrag.krankentaggeldversicherung: Daily sickness benefit of the insurance within the gross wage (CHF)
betrag.unfallversicherung: Daily accident benefit (UVG/SUVA) within the gross wage (CHF)
betrag.mutterschaftIv: Maternity or disability (IV) daily benefit within the gross wage (CHF)

betragHilfe.krankentaggeldversicherung: As on the insurer’s benefit statement. Tax-free, with no effect on the tax rate.
betragHilfe.beides: Only the insurance’s part as on the benefit statement. The employer’s top-up stays wage and is not deducted.
betragHilfe.unfallversicherung: Tax-free, but it raises the tax rate (progression clause).
betragHilfe.mutterschaftIv: Tax-free. The app does not fill the Anlage N-Gre’s own line for maternity and disability benefits yet: the amount is deducted like a daily sickness benefit for now, without the progression clause.

taggeld.lohnfortzahlung: Continued pay by the employer is wage: nothing is deducted.
taggeld.empfehlung: Recommended: daily sickness insurance, so deduct it. The AHV contributions in box 9 fit the wage without the benefit, which points to an insurance benefit, and that is tax-free. The choice is yours.
taggeld.widerspruch: This contradicts the wage statement: the AHV contributions in box 9 fit the wage without the benefit of {{betrag}}, which points to an insurance benefit. Choose continued pay only if the benefit statement or the monthly payslips show it (AHV-subject wage of the employer); otherwise tax-free money is taxed.

ahv.fits_without: Plausibility hint (not a decision): the contributions in Ziffer 9 ({{ziffer9}}) fit the gross wage without the daily benefit (AHV/IV/EO and ALV about {{ohne}}) better than with it (about {{mit}}), by {{abstand}}. That points to an insurance benefit, which is no AHV wage. Ziffer 9 can also hold the NBU premium; the benefit statement decides.
ahv.fits_with: Plausibility hint (not a decision): the contributions in Ziffer 9 ({{ziffer9}}) fit the gross wage with the daily benefit (AHV/IV/EO and ALV about {{mit}}) better than without it (about {{ohne}}), by {{abstand}}. That points to the money being paid as wage, i.e. continued pay by the employer. Ziffer 9 can also hold the NBU premium; the benefit statement decides.
ahv.too_close: Plausibility hint (not a decision): with and without the daily benefit the contributions in Ziffer 9 would be almost the same (about {{mit}} and {{ohne}}); they cannot tell the source apart.
ahv.nbu_likely: Plausibility hint (not a decision): Ziffer 9 ({{ziffer9}}) holds more than AHV/IV/EO and ALV on the whole gross wage (about {{mit}}), likely the NBU premium too; it does not show where the daily benefit came from.
ahv.fits_neither: Plausibility hint (not a decision): Ziffer 9 ({{ziffer9}}) is well below the contributions with the daily benefit (about {{mit}}) and without it (about {{ohne}}); it does not show where the daily benefit came from.

singleAssessment.text: For {{jahr}} you then file separate returns. The link with person B for {{jahr}} is released: what you entered for person B no longer belongs to your return, and an open invitation code stops working.

endPartnerLink.text: From {{jahr}} your partner no longer belongs to your household and you can no longer file a joint return. The years before stay as they are.

householdLeave.text: {{name}} no longer belongs to your household from {{jahr}}. The details on {{name}} from {{jahr}} are deleted; earlier years stay.

householdDelete.text: {{name}} disappears from every tax year, closed ones too. This cannot be undone.

lstbDiscardDraft.text: The values the owl read from your wage tax certificate are lost. Your saved details for {{jahr}} stay unchanged.

rentalRemoveRepair.text: The amount and its distribution are deleted from this property and no longer count as expenses.

childDelete.text: {{name}} and every detail on the child are deleted from {{jahr}}: child benefit, childcare costs and allowances drop out of your return.

bookingReverse.text: A counter-entry is posted. This is final: the booking and its reversal stay in the journal and cannot be deleted.

bookLock.text: This is final: bookings up to {{datum}} can then neither be changed nor reversed, and the lock cannot be lifted.

assetDispose.text: The asset counts as retired from the disposal date; the next depreciation run posts its remaining book value. This is final: only a reversal corrects it.

depreciationBook.text: The year's depreciation and disposals are posted to the journal. This is final: only a reversal corrects it.

openingBalance.text: The closing balance {{jahr}} is carried into {{folgejahr}} as the opening entry. This is final: it posts only once and only a reversal corrects it.

eBilanzSend.text: The E-Bilanz goes to your tax office. This is final: a transmitted E-Bilanz cannot be recalled, only replaced by a new one.

bankIgnore.text: The bank transaction is not booked and leaves the open list. A new import does not bring it back.

shareRemove.text: The share and its figures from the assessment notice are deleted and no longer count in your return.

proposalDiscard.text: The proposed value is lost; your current value stays.

partnerConsentWithdraw.text: From now on your partner no longer sees your details for {{jahr}} and cannot file {{jahr}} jointly with your figures. You can agree again later.

submissionWithdraw.text: The frozen version of your filed return {{jahr}} is released and the return counts as open again. Nothing changes at the tax office.

noteDelete.text: The note is gone; the owl no longer knows it in this conversation.

assistantRevoke.text: {{name}} loses access to your tax data at once. To connect again you have to grant access anew.
